title: Bounded completed cotangent torsion for a finite type algebra etale away from an ideal
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, and $S$ a finite type commutative $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Assume $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale over $\operatorname{Spec}A\setminus V(I)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Put $B=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}S/I^nS$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Then $B$ is Noetherian, is $IB$-adically complete, and $B/IB$ is finite type over $A/I$. There exists a surjective $A$-algebra map $P=\widehat{A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]}_I\twoheadrightarrow B$, for some $r\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. For every such presentation, with kernel $Q$, define the two-term complex $L_{B/A}^{\wedge}=(Q/Q^2\xrightarrow{\delta}B^{\oplus r})$ in degrees $-1,0$, where $\delta(\bar f)=(\partial f/\partial x_i\bmod Q)_i$ and partial derivatives on $P$ are the continuous extensions of polynomial differentiation. There is $c\geq0$ such that $I^c\ker\delta=I^c\operatorname{coker}\delta=0$. An ideal power annihilates a module here when each of its elements acts as zero through $A\to B$.

source.place: Tag 0ALQ (lemma-rig-etale), part (1), together with Tag 0AJU (lemma-equivalent-with-artin), condition (3); Tag 0AJQ (lemma-topologically-finite-type-Noetherian), parts (1) and (3), and Tag 0AJP (lemma-topologically-finite-type) supply the complete finite-type-reduction presentation.

proof.text: Because $S$ is finite type over the Noetherian ring $A$, it is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] to $S$ and the ideal $IS$ shows that $B=\varprojlim_n S/I^nS$ is Noetherian. The images in $S$ of a finite generating set for $I$ generate $IS$; such a set exists by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] identifies $B/IB$ with $S/IS$ and proves that $B$ is $IB$-adically complete. The quotient $S/IS$ is finite type over $A/I$ by the finite-type presentation, so the same holds for $B/IB$.

source.place: Tags 0AJQ (lemma-topologically-finite-type-Noetherian), parts (1) and (3), and 05GG for completeness and reduction modulo I

proof.text: Choose a finite polynomial presentation $\alpha:A[x_1,\ldots,x_s]\twoheadrightarrow S$ with finitely generated kernel $K$, using [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation]. The ordinary conormal map $d_\alpha:K/K^2\to S^{\oplus s}$ has a power $I^c$ annihilating both its kernel and cokernel by [lem-per-finite-type-jacobian-torsion-etale-away]. Independently, the complete finite-type reduction hypotheses from Step 1 give a finite restricted-polynomial presentation $\beta:P=\widehat{A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]}_I\twoheadrightarrow B$ for some $r\geq0$; this is the presentation-existence clause of [lem-per-completed-cotangent-transitivity] specialized to the identity map $B\to B$.

source.place: Tags 0ALQ(1), 0AJU(3), 0AJP and 0AJQ(3), which choose the ordinary and completed presentations

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-completed-jacobian-homology-comparison] to the ordinary presentation $\alpha$ and the arbitrary completed presentation $\beta$. It gives $\widehat{M}_1\cong\ker\delta$ and $\widehat{M}_0\cong\operatorname{coker}\delta$, where $M_1=\ker d_\alpha$, $M_0=\operatorname{coker}d_\alpha$, and $\delta$ is exactly the continuous partial-derivative map in the statement. Since $I^cM_i=0$, every quotient $M_i/I^nM_i$ is also killed by $I^c$, and therefore their inverse limits $\widehat M_i$ are killed by $I^c$. Transporting this annihilation across the two displayed isomorphisms proves $I^c\ker\delta=I^c\operatorname{coker}\delta=0$. The comparison applies to every choice of $\beta$, so the bound holds for every presentation.

source.place: Tag 0ALQ(1), together with Tag 0GAF (lemma-NL-is-completion), and the definition of the inverse-limit completion

proof.text: The map $\delta$ is well-defined because continuous polynomial differentiation is the completion of polynomial differentiation, as in the presentation comparison; its source and target are the two terms in degrees $-1$ and $0$ of the stated complex. Thus the preceding annihilation assertion is precisely the claimed bounded completed cotangent torsion, and Steps 1--3 establish all remaining clauses.
